chembl_bioactivity.bbvi_rule: bbvi.minimum_independent_mbpi_dois applies as min(link DOIs, ChEMBL documents) >= 2, so both the species link and the activity rest on two papers each.
chembl_bioactivity.cohort_rule: Cohort = every admitted ChEMBL activity with the same target_chembl_id and standard_type (activity level, counted with the ChEMBL API at the snapshot date). Species value = median pChEMBL of the parent compound's admitted activities in that cohort; percentile = 100 x (count below + 0.5 x count equal) / total.
chembl_bioactivity.commonness_rule: Exclude a compound when its count of taxa with a P703 statement exceeds the Tukey upper fence Q3 + 1.5 IQR of the counts over every linked compound (statistics.quantiles, n=4, inclusive). Such compounds (fatty acids, amino acids, sterols, carotenoids) say nothing specific about one species. Sensitivity: the same fence on log10 counts, and no filter.
chembl_bioactivity.drug_rule: Exclude compounds whose ChEMBL parent is an approved drug (max_phase 4): LOTUS text mining attaches reference drugs used as assay controls to the paper's organism (zidovudine -> Ecklonia cava, DOI 10.1016/j.bmc.2008.07.078). Natural products that are also approved drugs lose their link too. Sensitivity: no filter.
chembl_bioactivity.evidence_level: Reviewed original-paper strata (감태 ACE, AHTPDB peptides) are level 1; this automated stratum is level 2. The species MBPI is the max over all strata; the stratum of the best item is shown.
chembl_bioactivity.evidence_rule: link factor = 0.75 for one link DOI, 1.0 for two or more; activity factor = 0.75 for one ChEMBL document, 1.0 for two or more; evidence factor = link x activity. One item per species, parent compound and stratum: that compound's target x endpoint cohort with the highest percentile (ties: more records). The species MBPI is the highest adjusted item.

chembl_bioactivity.link_rule: Species -> compound: a Wikidata P703 (found in taxon) statement on the WoRMS accepted name or a WoRMS synonym with at least one P248 reference that has a DOI, or a verified original-paper link (paper_links) for species without P703 statements. References without a DOI are kept in the snapshot but do not count.
chembl_bioactivity.minimum_justification: Same as the peptide stratum: 30 peers keep one rank step at about 3 percentile points; below that a single record moves the score more than the 0.75 single-DOI discount.

trend.cell_rule: A record on a cell edge counts in every cell whose closed polygon holds it, as the OBIS statistics endpoint counts the effort; numerator and denominator use the same cells.
trend.cells: 1-degree cells where the species has a record in either period and its class has records in both periods
classes: undetermined: no comparable cell, fewer than min_past_records past records, a fall to ratio <= decline_ratio whose interval reaches 1, or a decline not confirmed within the dominant dataset
decline_signal: ratio <= decline_ratio (a 30% fall, IUCN criterion A2 VU threshold), interval below 1, and the same within the dominant dataset
decline_below_threshold: interval below 1 but the fall smaller than the threshold
survey_gap: fewer species records while class effort in the same cells also fell, and the reporting rate is not clearly lower
no_clear_decline: a reporting rate not lower
trend.dataset_check: A decline signal must also hold inside the dataset with most past records of the species (species and class records of that dataset only, same cells rule, same thresholds). Otherwise the fall may be a survey programme ending, and the class is undetermined. This is the reviewed-trend condition of docs/verified-indices-design.md, applied by rule to every species.
trend.effort: target group: OBIS records of the species' WoRMS class in the same cell and period; all-taxa records are a sensitivity
trend.formula: ratio = ((n_recent + 0.5) / E_recent) / ((n_past + 0.5) / E_past); 95% interval = ratio x/÷ exp(1.96 x sqrt(1/(n_past+0.5) + 1/(n_recent+0.5)))
trend.mcui_rule: A decline signal adds effort_adjustment (10) to a computed MCUI, capped at 100. Other classes add nothing. No class creates an MCUI for a species without an IUCN or national category, and none lowers one.

substitutes.not_used: AFCD Release 3 (FSANZ) food details carry no scientific names, so no AFCD row is matched to a genus or family; AFCD stays the oyster cross-check cohort.
substitutes.rule: Only a component missing from the species' own linked RDA row is filled, and only when that row reports at least one component. Candidates are uFiSh raw items of the consumed part fillet, flesh or muscle (not whole animal, organ or roe), per 100 g edible portion. Order: same-species RDA sub-sample rows (subsample_rule), then uFiSh WoRMS species or synonym, then same genus, then same family; within a level the higher grade factor, then larger n, then the lower item ID. A species-level value takes its grade from the uFiSh documentation code (a = measured 1.0; c, r, ar = calculated 0.85; e = proxy 0.5); every genus or family value is a proxy (0.5). Pooled entries spanning several families are never used.

substitutes.subsample_rule: Before any uFiSh value, a missing component is taken from other rows of the same RDA table that a review links to the same species and that the cohort rule excludes as sex or regional sub-samples (they never join the cohort). Rows whose main row is not species-specific (e.g. 고등어 남해/서해 under the generic 고등어 row) are not linked.

uncertainty: The cohort mixes molluscs, fish, crustaceans and a tunicate; ranks compare foods, not ecological or taxonomic peers.
Rows come from different source years and tables (domestic ('16), JAPAN('20), USDA('18)); per-value analysis method is not exposed.
Zinc is missing for most RDA seafood rows, so only foods reporting all three components can be ranked.
25-food fixed cohort: one rank step moves a nutrient percentile by about 4.0 points.
Sensitivity values are scenario arithmetic, not a statistical confidence interval.
